# df-script API Reference (v2.4.0)

> A zero-dependency, high-performance, expression-based DataFrame library for TypeScript/JavaScript.

- **License**: MIT
- **Website**: https://df-script.js.org
- **GitHub**: https://github.com/trentamorris/df-script
- **Overview (llms.txt)**: https://df-script.js.org/llms.txt
- **API Schema (docs.json)**: https://df-script.js.org/docs.json

# Column Expression API

## Namespace: $df.col.exprBase

## .alias()

Renames the output expression column key.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).alias(name: string): this
```

---

## .cast()

Coerces the column data type to another type.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).cast(
  dataType: RegisteredDataType,
  options: CastOptions = {}
): this
```

### Types Referenced
- [`RegisteredDataType`](#registereddatatype)
- [`CastOptions`](#castoptions)

---

## Namespace: $df.col.arrayExpr

## .agg()

Applies an aggregation expression or element-wise calculation over each array cell.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).arr.agg(expr: IExpr)
```

### Parameters
- `expr` (any): Aggregation expression (e.g. $df.element().sum() or $df.element().max())

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Types Referenced
- [`IExpr`](#iexpr)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5]] })
>>> df
shape: (2, 1)
+-----------+
| a         |
+-----------+
| [1, 2, 3] |
| [4, 5]    |
+-----------+
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("a").arr.agg($df.element().sum()).alias("sum_a"))
shape: (2, 2)
+-----------+-------+
| a         | sum_a |
+-----------+-------+
| [1, 2, 3] | 6     |
| [4, 5]    | 9     |
+-----------+-------+
```

---

## .all()

Returns true if all items in nested list cells are truthy.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).arr.all()
```

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5]] })
>>> df
shape: (2, 1)
+-----------+
| a         |
+-----------+
| [1, 2, 3] |
| [4, 5]    |
+-----------+
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("a").arr.all().alias("all_true"))
shape: (2, 2)
+---------------+----------+
| a             | all_true |
+---------------+----------+
| [true, true]  | true     |
| [true, false] | false    |
+---------------+----------+
```

---

## .any()

Returns true if any item in nested list cells is truthy.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).arr.any()
```

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5]] })
>>> df
shape: (2, 1)
+-----------+
| a         |
+-----------+
| [1, 2, 3] |
| [4, 5]    |
+-----------+
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("a").arr.any().alias("any_true"))
shape: (2, 2)
+---------------+----------+
| a             | any_true |
+---------------+----------+
| [true, true]  | true     |
| [true, false] | true     |
+---------------+----------+
```

---

## .argMax()

Finds the index of the maximum value in each array.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).arr.argMax()
```

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5]] })
>>> df
shape: (2, 1)
+-----------+
| a         |
+-----------+
| [1, 2, 3] |
| [4, 5]    |
+-----------+
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("a").arr.argMax().alias("max_idx"))
shape: (2, 2)
+-----------+---------+
| a         | max_idx |
+-----------+---------+
| [1, 2, 3] | 2       |
| [4, 5]    | 1       |
+-----------+---------+
```

---

## .contains()

Checks if nested lists contain item.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).arr.contains(item: any)
```

### Parameters
- `item` (any): The element to search for.

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5]] })
>>> df
shape: (2, 1)
+-----------+
| a         |
+-----------+
| [1, 2, 3] |
| [4, 5]    |
+-----------+
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("a").arr.contains(3).alias("has_three"))
shape: (2, 2)
+-----------+-----------+
| a         | has_three |
+-----------+-----------+
| [1, 2, 3] | true      |
| [4, 5]    | false     |
+-----------+-----------+
```

---

## .containsAll()

Checks if nested lists contain all elements in items.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).arr.containsAll(items: ArrayLike<any>)
```

### Parameters
- `items` (any): Array of elements that must all be present.

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5]] })
>>> df
shape: (2, 1)
+-----------+
| a         |
+-----------+
| [1, 2, 3] |
| [4, 5]    |
+-----------+
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("a").arr.containsAll([1, 2]).alias("has_all"))
shape: (2, 2)
+-----------+---------+
| a         | has_all |
+-----------+---------+
| [1, 2, 3] | true    |
| [4, 5]    | false   |
+-----------+---------+
```

---

## .containsAny()

Checks if nested lists contain any element in items.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).arr.containsAny(items: ArrayLike<any>)
```

### Parameters
- `items` (any): Array of elements where at least one must be present.

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5]] })
>>> df
shape: (2, 1)
+-----------+
| a         |
+-----------+
| [1, 2, 3] |
| [4, 5]    |
+-----------+
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("a").arr.containsAny([2, 3]).alias("has_any"))
shape: (2, 2)
+--------+---------+
| a      | has_any |
+--------+---------+
| [1, 2] | true    |
| [3, 4] | true    |
+--------+---------+
```

---

## .countMatches()

Counts occurrence frequency of item inside nested lists.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).arr.countMatches(
  item: any,
  options: UniqueArrayStatsOptions = {}
)
```

### Parameters
- `item` (any): The value to count occurrences of.
- `options` (any): Statistics and matching options.

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Types Referenced
- [`UniqueArrayStatsOptions`](#uniquearraystatsoptions)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5]] })
>>> df
shape: (2, 1)
+-----------+
| a         |
+-----------+
| [1, 2, 3] |
| [4, 5]    |
+-----------+
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("a").arr.countMatches(2).alias("twos"))
shape: (2, 2)
+-----------+------+
| a         | twos |
+-----------+------+
| [1, 2, 3] | 1    |
| [4, 5]    | 0    |
+-----------+------+
```

---

## .eval()

Evaluates subExpr element-wise across array lists.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).arr.eval(expr: IExpr)
```

### Parameters
- `expr` (any): The sub-expression to evaluate inside each nested list.

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Types Referenced
- [`IExpr`](#iexpr)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5]] })
>>> df
shape: (2, 1)
+-----------+
| a         |
+-----------+
| [1, 2, 3] |
| [4, 5]    |
+-----------+
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("a").arr.eval($df.element().mul(10)).alias("multiplied"))
shape: (2, 2)
+--------+------------+
| a      | multiplied |
+--------+------------+
| [1, 2] | [10, 20]   |
| [3, 4] | [30, 40]   |
+--------+------------+
```

---

## .explode()

Expands lists into row-wise elements and produces an index mapping for DataFrame unnesting.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).arr.explode(
  {
    emptyAsNull = true,
    keepNulls = true
  }: ExplodeOptions = {}
)
```

### Parameters
- `options` (any): Config options including handling of empty arrays and nulls.

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Types Referenced
- [`ExplodeOptions`](#explodeoptions)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5]] })
>>> df
shape: (2, 1)
+-----------+
| a         |
+-----------+
| [1, 2, 3] |
| [4, 5]    |
+-----------+
>>> df.select([$df.col("group"), $df.col("values").arr.explode()])
shape: (2, 2)
+-------+--------+
| group | values |
+-------+--------+
| A     | 1      |
| A     | 2      |
+-------+--------+
```

---

## .filter()

Filters elements of list columns matching a boolean sub-expression.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).arr.filter(expr: IExpr)
```

### Parameters
- `expr` (any): The boolean column expression to filter by.

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Types Referenced
- [`IExpr`](#iexpr)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5]] })
>>> df
shape: (2, 1)
+-----------+
| a         |
+-----------+
| [1, 2, 3] |
| [4, 5]    |
+-----------+
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("a").arr.filter($df.element().gt(2)).alias("filtered"))
shape: (2, 2)
+-----------+----------+
| a         | filtered |
+-----------+----------+
| [1, 2, 3] | [3]      |
| [4, 5]    | [4, 5]   |
+-----------+----------+
```

---

## .first()

Returns the first element of each list.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).arr.first(nullOnOob: boolean = true)
```

### Parameters
- `nullOnOob` (any): If true, returns null if the list is empty (default: true).

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5]] })
>>> df
shape: (2, 1)
+-----------+
| a         |
+-----------+
| [1, 2, 3] |
| [4, 5]    |
+-----------+
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("a").arr.first().alias("first_a"))
shape: (2, 2)
+-----------+---------+
| a         | first_a |
+-----------+---------+
| [1, 2, 3] | 1       |
| [4, 5]    | 4       |
+-----------+---------+
```

---

## .gather()

Gathers specific indices from each nested list.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).arr.gather(
  indices: number | ArrayLike<number>,
  nullOnOob: boolean = true
)
```

### Parameters
- `indices` (any): Index or array of indices to extract.
- `nullOnOob` (any): If true, returns null for indices out of bounds (default: true).

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5]] })
>>> df
shape: (2, 1)
+-----------+
| a         |
+-----------+
| [1, 2, 3] |
| [4, 5]    |
+-----------+
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("a").arr.gather([0, 2]).alias("g"))
shape: (2, 2)
+-----------+----------+
| a         | g        |
+-----------+----------+
| [1, 2, 3] | [1, 3]   |
| [4, 5]    | [4, null]|
+-----------+----------+
```

---

## .gatherEvery()

Gather element slices with custom steps.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).arr.gatherEvery(options: StepSliceArrayOptions = {})
```

### Parameters
- `options` (any): Config options including offset, limit, and step size.

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Types Referenced
- [`StepSliceArrayOptions`](#stepslicearrayoptions)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5]] })
>>> df
shape: (2, 1)
+-----------+
| a         |
+-----------+
| [1, 2, 3] |
| [4, 5]    |
+-----------+
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("a").arr.gatherEvery({ step: 2 }).alias("ge"))
shape: (2, 2)
+-----------+--------+
| a         | ge     |
+-----------+--------+
| [1, 2, 3] | [1, 3] |
| [4, 5]    | [4]    |
+-----------+--------+
```

---

## .get()

Extracts a single list element by its index position.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).arr.get(
  index: number,
  nullOnOob: boolean = true
)
```

### Parameters
- `index` (any): The 0-based or negative index position to extract.
- `nullOnOob` (any): If true, returns null if index is out of bounds (default: true).

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5]] })
>>> df
shape: (2, 1)
+-----------+
| a         |
+-----------+
| [1, 2, 3] |
| [4, 5]    |
+-----------+
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("a").arr.get(1).alias("second"))
shape: (2, 2)
+-----------+--------+
| a         | second |
+-----------+--------+
| [1, 2, 3] | 2      |
| [4, 5]    | 5      |
+-----------+--------+
```

---

## .join()

Joins elements of list columns into a single string column.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).arr.join(
  separator: string = ",",
  options: JoinArrayOptions = {}
)
```

### Parameters
- `separator` (any): The character sequence separating list elements.
- `options` (any): String conversion options.

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Types Referenced
- [`JoinArrayOptions`](#joinarrayoptions)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5]] })
>>> df
shape: (2, 1)
+-----------+
| a         |
+-----------+
| [1, 2, 3] |
| [4, 5]    |
+-----------+
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("a").arr.join("-").alias("joined"))
shape: (2, 2)
+------------+--------+
| a          | joined |
+------------+--------+
| ["a", "b"] | "a-b"  |
| ["c"]      | "c"    |
+------------+--------+
```

---

## .last()

Returns the last element of each list.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).arr.last(nullOnOob: boolean = true)
```

### Parameters
- `nullOnOob` (any): If true, returns null if the list is empty (default: true).

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5]] })
>>> df
shape: (2, 1)
+-----------+
| a         |
+-----------+
| [1, 2, 3] |
| [4, 5]    |
+-----------+
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("a").arr.last().alias("last_a"))
shape: (2, 2)
+-----------+--------+
| a         | last_a |
+-----------+--------+
| [1, 2, 3] | 3      |
| [4, 5]    | 5      |
+-----------+--------+
```

## .reverse()

Reverses elements of list columns.

### Signature
```typescript

```

```typescript
+-----------+

+-----------+

+-----------+-----------+

| [1, 2, 3] | [3, 2, 1] |
| [4, 5]    | [5, 4]    |
+-----------+-----------+
```

## .shift()

Shifts elements of list columns by N offsets.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).arr.shift(
  n: number = 1,
  options: ShiftOptions = {}
)
```

### Parameters
- `n` (any): Positive or negative offsets shift amount (default: 1).

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Types Referenced
- [`ShiftOptions`](#shiftoptions)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5]] })
>>> df
shape: (2, 1)
+-----------+
| a         |
+-----------+
| [1, 2, 3] |
| [4, 5]    |
+-----------+
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("a").arr.shift(1).alias("shifted"))
shape: (2, 2)
+-----------+------------------+
| a         | shifted          |
+-----------+------------------+
| [1, 2, 3] | [null, 1, 2]     |
| [4, 5]    | [null, 4]        |
+-----------+------------------+
```

---

## .slice()

Slices nested list arrays.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).arr.slice(
  start?: number,
  end?: number
)
```

### Parameters
- `start` (any): The slice starting index.
- `end` (any): The slice ending index.

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5]] })
>>> df
shape: (2, 1)
+-----------+
| a         |
+-----------+
| [1, 2, 3] |
| [4, 5]    |
+-----------+
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("a").arr.slice(1, 3).alias("sliced"))
shape: (2, 2)
+-----------+--------+
| a         | sliced |
+-----------+--------+
| [1, 2, 3] | [2, 3] |
| [4, 5]    | [5]    |
+-----------+--------+
```

---

## .sort()

Sorts elements inside each list.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).arr.sort(options?: SortArrayOptions)
```

### Parameters

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Types Referenced
- [`SortArrayOptions`](#sortarrayoptions)

### Examples
```typescript

+-----------+
| [1, 2, 3] |
| [4, 5]    |
```

```typescript
  start: number,
  deleteCount?: number,
  ...items: any[]
)
```

### Parameters

- `deleteCount` (any): The number of elements to remove.
- `items` (any): The elements to insert.

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Examples
```typescript

>>> df

+-----------+

| [4, 5]    |

+-----------+-----------------+
| [1, 2, 3] | [1, 10, 20, 3]  |
| [4, 5]    | [4, 10, 20]     |
+-----------+-----------------+
```

```typescript
+-------+-------+---------+

```

```typescript
| group | val |
+-------+-----+
| A     | 10  |
| A     | 20  |
| B     | 30  |

| B     | 30   |
+-------+------+
```

## .between()

Checks if values fall inside lower and upper boundaries (inclusive).

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).between(
  lower: any,
  upper: any,
  closed: "both" | "left" | "right" | "none" = "both"
)
```

### Parameters
- `lower` (any): The lower boundary value or expression.
- `upper` (any): The upper boundary value or expression.
- `closed` (any): Control boundary inclusivity: "both", "left", "right", or "none" (default: "both").

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [1, 2, 3], b: [10, 20, 30] })
>>> df
shape: (3, 2)
+---+----+
| a | b  |
+---+----+
| 1 | 10 |
| 2 | 20 |
| 3 | 30 |
+---+----+
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("a").between(1, 2).alias("in_range"))
shape: (3, 3)
+---+----+----------+
| a | b  | in_range |
+---+----+----------+
| 1 | 10 | true     |
| 2 | 20 | true     |
| 3 | 30 | false    |
+---+----+----------+
```

## .copysign()

Returns absolute value of expr with the sign of other.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).copysign(val: NumericArg)
```

### Parameters
- `val` (any): The sign source value or column expression.

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Types Referenced
- [`NumericArg`](#numericarg)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [1, 2, 3], b: [10, 20, 30] })
>>> df

+---+----+
| a | b  |
+---+----+
| 1 | 10 |
| 2 | 20 |
| 3 | 30 |
+---+----+
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("a").copysign($df.col("b")).alias("signed"))
shape: (3, 3)
+---+----+--------+
| a | b  | signed |
+---+----+--------+
| 1 | 10 | 1      |
| 2 | 20 | 2      |
| 3 | 30 | 3      |
+---+----+--------+
```

## .count()

Aggregation: Returns the count of records inside the group.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).count(options: { includeNulls?: boolean } = {})
```

### Parameters
- `options` (any): Config flags including whether to count null values.

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ group: ["A", "A", "B"], val: [10, 20, 30] })
>>> df
shape: (3, 2)
+-------+-----+
| group | val |
+-------+-----+
| A     | 10  |
| A     | 20  |
| B     | 30  |
+-------+-----+
>>> df.groupBy("group").agg($df.col("val").count().alias("cnt"))
shape: (2, 2)
+-------+-----+
| group | cnt |
+-------+-----+
| A     | 2   |
| B     | 1   |
+-------+-----+
```

## .eqMissing()

```typescript
| null | 2    |

| null | true       |
| 3    | false      |
+------+------------+
```

## .fill()

Replaces targeted values ("null", "nan", or "all") with a specified value or strategy.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).fill(
  target: FillTarget,
  options: FillOptions | ValidScalarTypes | IExpr = {}
): this
```

### Parameters
- `target` (any): The target value type to replace: "null", "nan", or "all".
- `options` (any): Configuration options including replacement value, strategy, and optional limit, or a replacement scalar/expression directly.

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Types Referenced
- [`FillTarget`](#filltarget)
- [`FillOptions`](#filloptions)
- [`ValidScalarTypes`](#validscalartypes)
- [`IExpr`](#iexpr)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [1, null, 3], b: [null, 2, null] })
>>> df
shape: (3, 2)
+------+------+
| a    | b    |
+------+------+
| 1    | null |
| null | 2    |
| 3    | null |
+------+------+
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("a").fill("null", { value: 0 }).alias("filled"))
shape: (3, 2)
+------+--------+
| a    | filled |
+------+--------+
| 1    | 1      |
| null | 0      |
| 3    | 3      |
+------+--------+
```

## .first()

Aggregation: Finds the first value in the group.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).first()
```

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ group: ["A", "A", "B"], val: [10, 20, 30] })
>>> df
shape: (3, 2)
+-------+-----+
| group | val |
+-------+-----+
| A     | 10  |
| A     | 20  |
| B     | 30  |
+-------+-----+
>>> df.groupBy("group").agg($df.col("val").first().alias("first_val"))
shape: (2, 2)
+-------+-----------+
| group | first_val |
+-------+-----------+
| A     | 10        |
| B     | 30        |
+-------+-----------+
```

## .hypot()

```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).hypot(val: NumericArg)
```

- `val` (any): The other numeric value or column expression.

- [`NumericArg`](#numericarg)

## .implode()

Aggregation: Combines all values in the group into a single array/list cell.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).implode()
```

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ group: ["A", "A", "B"], val: [10, 20, 30] })
>>> df
shape: (3, 2)
+-------+-----+
| group | val |
+-------+-----+
| A     | 10  |
| A     | 20  |
| B     | 30  |
+-------+-----+
>>> df.groupBy("group").agg($df.col("val").implode().alias("list_val"))
shape: (2, 2)
+-------+----------+
| group | list_val |
+-------+----------+
| A     | [10, 20] |
| B     | [30]     |
+-------+----------+
```

```typescript
)
```

```typescript
| 3 | false |
+---+-------+
```

## .isNDistinct()

Checks if column values match the N-th distinct value by positive or negative index position.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).isNDistinct(
  index: number,
  nullOnOob: boolean = true
)
```

### Parameters
- `index` (any): The 0-based or negative index position into the ordered distinct values (e.g. 0 for first distinct, -1 for last distinct).
- `nullOnOob` (any): If true, returns null if index is out of bounds (default: true).

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [1, 2, 3], b: [10, 20, 30] })
>>> df
shape: (3, 2)
+---+----+
| a | b  |
+---+----+
| 1 | 10 |
| 2 | 20 |
| 3 | 30 |
+---+----+
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("a").isNDistinct(0).alias("is_first"))
shape: (3, 3)
+---+----+----------+
| a | b  | is_first |
+---+----+----------+
| 1 | 10 | true     |
| 2 | 20 | false    |
| 3 | 30 | false    |
+---+----+----------+
```

## .lag()

Window: Shifts values down by offset, filling missing slots with default value.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).lag(
  offset: number = 1,
  options: ShiftOptions = {}
)
```

### Parameters
- `offset` (any): Number of rows to shift down (default 1).
- `options` (any): Shift options configuring fallback fillValue (default null).

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Types Referenced
- [`ShiftOptions`](#shiftoptions)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [1, 2, 3] })
>>> df
shape: (3, 1)
+---+
| a |
+---+
| 1 |
| 2 |
| 3 |
+---+
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("val").lag(1, { fillValue: 0 }).alias("prev"))
shape: (3, 2)
+-----+------+
| val | prev |
+-----+------+
| 10  | 0    |
| 20  | 10   |
| 30  | 20   |
+-----+------+
```

```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).minBy(by: any)
```

### Parameters
- `by` (any): Column or expression to order by.

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ group: ["A", "A", "B"], val: [10, 20, 30] })
>>> df
shape: (3, 2)
+-------+-----+
| group | val |
+-------+-----+
| A     | 10  |
| A     | 20  |
| B     | 30  |
+-------+-----+
>>> df.select($df.col("group").minBy($df.col("val")).alias("lowest_group"))
shape: (1, 1)
+--------------+
| lowest_group |
+--------------+
| A            |
+--------------+
```

```typescript
| null | false       |
| 3    | true        |
+------+-------------+
```

## .over()

Executes a window aggregation partitioned by column keys.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).over(columns: string | IExpr | (string | IExpr)[])
```

### Parameters
- `columns` (any): Column expression or array of columns to partition by.

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Types Referenced
- [`IExpr`](#iexpr)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ group: ["A", "A", "B"], val: [10, 20, 30] })
>>> df
shape: (3, 2)
+-------+-----+
| group | val |
+-------+-----+
| A     | 10  |
| A     | 20  |
| B     | 30  |
+-------+-----+
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("val").sum().over("group").alias("cat_sum"))
shape: (3, 3)
+-------+-----+---------+
| group | val | cat_sum |
+-------+-----+---------+
| A     | 10  | 30      |
| A     | 20  | 30      |
| B     | 30  | 30      |
+-------+-----+---------+
```

## .product()

```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).product()
```

## .rolling()

Window: Computes a rolling window reduction using a ColumnExpression or a custom callback function.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).rolling(
  optionsOrWindowSize: number | RollingOptions,
  exprOrFn: IExpr | ((vals: any[]) => any)
)
```

### Parameters
- `optionsOrWindowSize` (any): Window row count or RollingOptions configuration.
- `exprOrFn` (any): ColumnExpression to evaluate over each window slice, or a custom reducer function.

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Types Referenced
- [`RollingOptions`](#rollingoptions)
- [`IExpr`](#iexpr)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [1, 2, 3] })
>>> df
shape: (3, 1)
+---+
| a |
+---+
| 1 |
| 2 |
| 3 |
+---+
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("val").rolling(2, $df.col("val").sum()).alias("r_sum"))
shape: (3, 2)
+-----+-------+
| val | r_sum |
+-----+-------+
| 10  | 10    |
| 20  | 30    |
| 30  | 50    |
+-----+-------+
```

---

- `decimals` (any): Number of decimal places to round to (default: 0).

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Types Referenced
- [`RoundOptions`](#roundoptions)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [1, 2, 3] })
>>> df
shape: (3, 1)
+---+
| a |
+---+
| 1 |
| 2 |
| 3 |
+---+
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("a").round(1).alias("rounded"))
shape: (3, 2)
+---+---------+
| a | rounded |
+---+---------+
| 1 | 1       |
| 2 | 2       |
| 3 | 3       |
+---+---------+
```

## .rowNumber()

Window: Computes 1-indexed row number count within group partitions.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).rowNumber()
```

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ group: ["A", "A", "B"], val: [10, 20, 30] })
>>> df
shape: (3, 2)
+-------+-----+
| group | val |
+-------+-----+
| A     | 10  |
| A     | 20  |
| B     | 30  |
+-------+-----+
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("val").rowNumber().over("group").alias("rn"))
shape: (3, 3)
+-------+-----+----+
| group | val | rn |
+-------+-----+----+
| A     | 10  | 1  |
| A     | 20  | 2  |
| B     | 30  | 1  |
+-------+-----+----+
```

---

## .shift()

Shifts values by the given number of rows, filling newly introduced slots with null. Positive offsets shift values down (lag); negative offsets shift values up (lead).

Supports windowing and partition grouping via `.over(...)`.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).shift(
  n: number = 1,
  options: ShiftOptions = {}
)
```

### Parameters
- `n` (any): Number of rows to shift (positive for down, negative for up). Default 1.

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Types Referenced
- [`ShiftOptions`](#shiftoptions)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [1, 2, 3] })
>>> df
shape: (3, 1)
+---+
| a |
+---+
| 1 |
| 2 |
| 3 |
+---+
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("a").shift(1).alias("shifted"))
shape: (3, 2)
+---+---------+
| a | shifted |
+---+---------+
| 1 | null    |
| 2 | 1       |
| 3 | 2       |
+---+---------+
```

---

## .sum()

```typescript

```

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Examples
```typescript

| group | val |
+-------+-----+
| A     | 10  |
| A     | 20  |
| B     | 30  |
+-------+-----+
>>> df.groupBy("group").agg($df.col("val").sum().alias("total"))

+-------+-------+
| group | total |
+-------+-------+
| A     | 30    |
| B     | 30    |
+-------+-------+
```

## .extract()

Extracts a captured group from the first regex match.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).str.extract(
  pattern: RegExp | string,
  options?: ExtractRegexEngineOptions
)
```

### Parameters
- `pattern` (any): The regex pattern containing capture groups.
- `options` (any): Options object. Use `groupIndex` to select the group (default 1).

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Types Referenced
- [`ExtractRegexEngineOptions`](#extractregexengineoptions)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ s: ["apple", "banana", "cherry"] })
>>> df
shape: (3, 1)
+----------+
| s        |
+----------+
| "apple"  |
| "banana" |
| "cherry" |
+----------+
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("email").str.extract(/@(\w+)/).alias("domain"))
shape: (2, 2)
+------------------+---------+
| email            | domain  |
+------------------+---------+
| user@example.com | example |
| admin@test.org   | test    |
+------------------+---------+
```

## .extractAll()

Extracts all occurrences matching a regular expression pattern.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).str.extractAll(
  pattern: string | RegExp,
  options?: ExtractRegexEngineOptions
)
```

### Parameters
- `pattern` (any): Search pattern (string or RegExp).
- `options` (any): Options object. Use `groupIndex` to select the group (default 0).

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Types Referenced
- [`ExtractRegexEngineOptions`](#extractregexengineoptions)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ s: ["apple", "banana", "cherry"] })
>>> df
shape: (3, 1)
+----------+
| s        |
+----------+
| "apple"  |
| "banana" |
| "cherry" |
+----------+
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("s").str.extractAll(/[aeiou]/).alias("vowels"))
shape: (3, 2)
+----------+-----------------+
| s        | vowels          |
+----------+-----------------+
| "apple"  | ["a", "e"]      |
| "banana" | ["a", "a", "a"] |
| "cherry" | ["e"]           |
+----------+-----------------+
```

## .extractGroups()

Extracts all captured groups from the first regex match into a structured object (struct).

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).str.extractGroups(
  pattern: string | RegExp,
  options: ExtractRegexEngineOptions = {}
)
```

### Parameters
- `pattern` (any): Search pattern containing capture groups.

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Types Referenced
- [`ExtractRegexEngineOptions`](#extractregexengineoptions)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ s: ["apple", "banana", "cherry"] })
>>> df
shape: (3, 1)
+----------+
| s        |
+----------+
| "apple"  |
| "banana" |
| "cherry" |
+----------+
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("email").str.extractGroups(/(?<user>\w+)@(?<domain>\w+)/).alias("parsed"))
shape: (2, 2)
+------------------+------------------------------------+
| email            | parsed                             |
+------------------+------------------------------------+
| user@example.com | { user: "user", domain: "example" }|
| admin@test.org   | { user: "admin", domain: "test" }  |
+------------------+------------------------------------+
```

## .replaceMany()

Replaces multiple string patterns simultaneously or sequentially with their respective replacements. Matches Polars `.str.replaceMany()` behavior, accepting pattern/replacement arrays or a pattern-to-replacement map dictionary.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).str.replaceMany(
  patterns: (string | RegExp)[] | Record<string, string>,
  replacements?: (string | ((match: string, ...args: any[]) => string))[],
  options?: ReplaceManyOptions
)
```

### Parameters
- `patterns` (any): Array of patterns or an object mapping target patterns to replacements.
- `replacements` (any): Array of replacement strings/callbacks (when patterns is an array).
- `options` (any): Configuration options ({ literal, asciiCaseInsensitive, mode }).

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Types Referenced
- [`ReplaceManyOptions`](#replacemanyoptions)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ s: ["apple", "banana", "cherry"] })
>>> df
shape: (3, 1)
+----------+
| s        |
+----------+
| "apple"  |
| "banana" |
| "cherry" |
+----------+
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("s").str.replaceMany(["apple", "banana"], ["1", "2"]).alias("res"))
shape: (3, 2)
+----------+--------+
| s        | res    |
+----------+--------+
| "apple"  | 1      |
| "banana" | 2      |
| "cherry" | cherry |
+----------+--------+
```

```typescript
| "apple"  |
| "banana" |
| "cherry" |
+----------+
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("s").str.stripChars().alias("stripped"))
shape: (2, 2)
+-------------+----------+
| s           | stripped |
+-------------+----------+
| "  hello  " | hello    |
| "  world  " | world    |
+-------------+----------+
```

## Namespace: $df.col.structExpr

## .field()

Extracts a sub-field property value from nested objects/struct columns.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).struct.field(name: string)
```

### Parameters
- `name` (any): Name of the field key to extract.

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ user: [{ name: "Alice", age: 30 }] })
>>> df
shape: (1, 1)
+--------------------------------+
| user                           |
+--------------------------------+
| { name: "Alice", age: 30 }     |
+--------------------------------+
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("user").struct.field("name").alias("user_name"))
shape: (1, 2)
+---------------------------+-----------+
| user                      | user_name |
+---------------------------+-----------+
| { name: "Alice", id: 1 }  | Alice     |
+---------------------------+-----------+
```

## .renameFields()

Renames existing field keys inside structured object columns.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).struct.renameFields(mapping: Record<string, string>)
```

### Parameters
- `mapping` (any): Key-value map of current field names to new field names.

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ user: [{ name: "Alice", age: 30 }] })
>>> df
shape: (1, 1)
+--------------------------------+
| user                           |
+--------------------------------+
| { name: "Alice", age: 30 }     |
+--------------------------------+
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("user").struct.renameFields({ name: "first_name" }).alias("user_renamed"))
shape: (1, 2)
+---------------------------+--------------------------------+
| user                      | user_renamed                   |
+---------------------------+--------------------------------+
| { name: "Alice", id: 1 }  | { id: 1, first_name: "Alice" } |
+---------------------------+--------------------------------+
```

## .withFields()

```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).struct.withFields(fields: IntoExpr[] | Record<string, IntoExpr>)
```

### Parameters
- `fields` (any): Expressions or field map defining new or updated fields.

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Types Referenced
- [`IntoExpr`](#intoexpr)

### Examples

```typescript
+--------------------------------+
| user                           |
+--------------------------------+
| { name: "Alice", age: 30 }     |
+--------------------------------+

+------------------------------+-------------------------------------------+
| user                         | updated_user                              |
```

## Namespace: $df.col.temporalExpr

## .castTimeUnit()

Casts the schema time unit of a Datetime column (`"ms"`, `"us"`, `"ns"`). This is a metadata-only operation — underlying millisecond Date timestamps are preserved.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).dt.castTimeUnit(unit: DatetimeTimeUnit)
```

### Parameters
- `unit` (any): Target time unit: `"ms"` (milliseconds), `"us"` (microseconds), or `"ns"` (nanoseconds).

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Types Referenced
- [`DatetimeTimeUnit`](#datetimetimeunit)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ date: ["2026-05-20T10:00:00.123Z"] })
>>> df
shape: (1, 1)
+--------------------------+
| date                     |
+--------------------------+
| 2026-05-20T10:00:00.123Z |
+--------------------------+
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("ts").dt.castTimeUnit("us").alias("ts_us"))
shape: (1, 2)
+--------------------------+--------------------------+
| ts                       | ts_us                    |
+--------------------------+--------------------------+
| 2026-05-20T10:00:00.123Z | 2026-05-20T10:00:00.123Z |
+--------------------------+--------------------------+
```

---

## .century()

Extracts the 1-indexed century component (e.g. 21 for 2026) from a Datetime column.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).dt.century(timeZone?: string)
```

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ date: ["2026-05-20T10:00:00.123Z"] })
>>> df
shape: (1, 1)
+--------------------------+
| date                     |
+--------------------------+
| 2026-05-20T10:00:00.123Z |
+--------------------------+
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("d").dt.century().alias("century"))
shape: (1, 2)
+------------+---------+
| d          | century |
+------------+---------+
| 2026-05-20 | 21      |
+------------+---------+
```

---

## .convertTimeZone()

Converts a Datetime column to a different IANA timezone. Preserves the exact UTC epoch instant while changing the timezone label, affecting how local wall-clock component extractors (`hour()`, `day()`, etc.) and `strftime` interpret values. Requires the column to already be timezone-aware; use `replace({ timeZone })` to assign a timezone to a naive column first.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).dt.convertTimeZone(timeZone: string)
```

### Parameters
- `timeZone` (any): Target IANA timezone identifier (e.g. `"UTC"`, `"America/New_York"`, `"Europe/London"`).

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ date: ["2026-05-20T10:00:00.123Z"] })
>>> df
shape: (1, 1)
+--------------------------+
| date                     |
+--------------------------+
| 2026-05-20T10:00:00.123Z |
+--------------------------+
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("ts").dt.replace({ timeZone: "UTC" }).dt.convertTimeZone("America/New_York").alias("ts_ny"))
shape: (1, 2)
+--------------------------+-------------------------------+
| ts                       | ts_ny                         |
+--------------------------+-------------------------------+
| 2026-05-20T10:00:00.123Z | 2026-05-20 06:00:00.123 EDT   |
+--------------------------+-------------------------------+
```

## .replace()

Replaces specific date and time components (`year`, `month`, `day`, `hour`, `minute`, `second`, `ms`, `timeZone`) of a Datetime column. Unspecified components are preserved from the original value. When `timeZone` is provided in options, components are interpreted in that timezone. Note: `month` is 1-indexed (1 = January, 12 = December); `day` is 1-indexed (1-31).

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).dt.replace(options: ReplaceDateOptions)
```

### Parameters
- `options` (any): Object specifying which components to replace.

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Types Referenced
- [`ReplaceDateOptions`](#replacedateoptions)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ date: ["2026-05-20T10:00:00.123Z"] })
>>> df
shape: (1, 1)
+--------------------------+
| date                     |
+--------------------------+
| 2026-05-20T10:00:00.123Z |
+--------------------------+
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("ts").dt.replace({ year: 2030, month: 1, day: 1 }).alias("replaced"))
shape: (1, 2)
+--------------------------+--------------------------+
| ts                       | replaced                 |
+--------------------------+--------------------------+
| 2026-05-20T10:00:00.123Z | 2030-01-01T10:00:00.123Z |
+--------------------------+--------------------------+
```

---

## .strftime()

Formats Datetime values into custom formatted strings using strftime directive pattern tokens. Automatically applies the column's assigned timezone unless explicitly overridden in options.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).dt.strftime(options: StrftimeOptions)
```

### Parameters
- `options` (any): Formatting pattern string (e.g. `"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"`) or configuration object.

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Types Referenced
- [`StrftimeOptions`](#strftimeoptions)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ date: ["2026-05-20T10:00:00.123Z"] })
>>> df
shape: (1, 1)
+--------------------------+
| date                     |
+--------------------------+
| 2026-05-20T10:00:00.123Z |
+--------------------------+
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("d").dt.strftime("%Y/%m/%d").alias("formatted"))
shape: (1, 2)
+------------+------------+
| d          | formatted  |
+------------+------------+
| 2026-05-20 | 2026/05/20 |
+------------+------------+
```

## .totalDays()

Converts Duration to floating point minutes.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).dt.totalMinutes()
```

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ date: ["2026-05-20T10:00:00.123Z"] })
>>> df
shape: (1, 1)
+--------------------------+
| date                     |
+--------------------------+
| 2026-05-20T10:00:00.123Z |
+--------------------------+
>>> df.withColumns($df.duration({ days: $df.col("add") }).dt.totalMinutes().alias("mins"))
shape: (2, 3)
+------------+-----+------+
| dt         | add | mins |
+------------+-----+------+
| 2026-01-01 | 1   | 1440 |
| 2026-01-01 | 2   | 2880 |
+------------+-----+------+
```

---

## .utcOffset()

Returns the UTC offset of a timezone for a given Datetime value. Supports returning the total offset, the standard (base) offset, or just the daylight saving time component, in multiple output formats.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.col(<column_name>).dt.utcOffset(
  timeZone?: string,
  options: UtcOffsetOptions = {}
)
```

### Parameters
- `timeZone` (any): Optional IANA timezone identifier. Defaults to the system local timezone.
- `options` (any): Output configuration: `type` selects which offset component to return (`"total"` | `"standardTime"` | `"daylightSavingTime"`), and `format` controls the output unit (`"milliseconds"` | `"minutes"` | `"hours"` | `"iso"` | `"basic"`).

### Returns: `ColumnExpression`

### Types Referenced
- [`UtcOffsetOptions`](#utcoffsetoptions)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ date: ["2026-05-20T10:00:00.123Z"] })
>>> df
shape: (1, 1)
+--------------------------+
| date                     |
+--------------------------+
| 2026-05-20T10:00:00.123Z |
+--------------------------+
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("d").dt.utcOffset("UTC").alias("offset"))
shape: (1, 2)
+------------+--------+
| d          | offset |
+------------+--------+
| 2026-05-20 | 0      |
+------------+--------+
```

---

```typescript
+------------+------+

+------------+------+
```

# DataFrame API

## .cast()

Casts columns in the DataFrame to the specified data type(s).

### Signature
```typescript
df.cast(
  dtypes: RegisteredDataType | Record<string, RegisteredDataType>,
  options: CastOptions = {}
): DataFrame<any>
```

### Parameters
- `dtypes` (RegisteredDataType | Record<string, RegisteredDataType>): Target data type for all columns, or mapping of column names to target data types.
- `[options]` (CastOptions): Casting options (e.g. strict).

### Returns: `DataFrame`

### Types Referenced
- [`RegisteredDataType`](#registereddatatype)
- [`CastOptions`](#castoptions)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [1, 2], b: ["x", "y"] })
>>> df
shape: (2, 2)
+---+---+
| a | b |
+---+---+
| 1 | x |
| 2 | y |
+---+---+
>>> df.cast($df.Float64)
>>> df.cast({ a: $df.Float64, b: $df.Utf8 })
>>> df.cast({ num_str: $df.Int64 }, { strict: false })
```

---

## .clone()

Creates a deep copy of the current DataFrame instance, duplicating all underlying column data arrays and schema metadata. Modifying columns or values in the cloned DataFrame will not mutate the original.

### Signature
```typescript
df.clone(): DataFrame<T>
```

### Returns: `DataFrame<T>`

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [1, 2], b: ["x", "y"] })
>>> df
shape: (2, 2)
+---+---+
| a | b |
+---+---+
| 1 | x |
| 2 | y |
+---+---+
```

---

## .columns

Gets array of column names in the DataFrame.

### Signature
```typescript
df.columns: string[]
```

### Returns: `Array of column name strings.`

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [1, 2], b: ["x", "y"] })
>>> df
shape: (2, 2)
+---+---+
| a | b |
+---+---+
| 1 | x |
| 2 | y |
+---+---+
>>> df.columns
["a", "b"]
```

---

## .concat()

Concatenates items vertically, horizontally, or diagonally.

### Signature
```typescript
df.concat<U extends RowRecord = any>(
  items: ConcatItem | ConcatItem[],
  options: ConcatOptions = {}
): DataFrame<U>
```

### Parameters
- `items` (ConcatItem | ConcatItem[]): Single DataFrame or array of DataFrames/rows to concatenate.
- `[options]` (ConcatOptions): Configuration options for concatenation layout and strictness.
- `[options.how]` (ConcatHow): Layout strategy: `"vertical"` (default, appends rows top-to-bottom), `"horizontal"` (joins unique columns side-by-side), or `"diagonal"` (concatenates mismatched columns with null padding).
- `[options.horizontal.strict]` (boolean): When `true` (default), throws an error if row counts mismatch in horizontal concatenation. Set `false` to pad shorter DataFrames with `null`.

### Returns: `DataFrame`

### Types Referenced
- [`RowRecord`](#rowrecord)
- [`ConcatItem`](#concatitem)
- [`ConcatOptions`](#concatoptions)

### Examples
```typescript
// 1. Vertical Concatenation (default):
>>> const df1 = $df.data({ a: [1, 2] })
>>> const df2 = $df.data({ b: [10, 20] })
>>> df1
shape: (2, 1)
+---+
| a |
+---+
| 1 |
| 2 |
+---+
>>> df2
shape: (2, 1)
+----+
| b  |
+----+
| 10 |
| 20 |
+----+
>>> df1.concat(df2, { how: "vertical" })
shape: (4, 1)
+------+
| a    |
+------+
| 1    |
| 2    |
| null |
| null |
+------+

// 2. Horizontal Concatenation:
>>> const df1 = $df.data({ a: [1, 2] })
>>> const df2 = $df.data({ b: [10, 20] })
>>> df1
shape: (2, 1)
+---+
| a |
+---+
| 1 |
| 2 |
+---+
>>> df2
shape: (2, 1)
+----+
| b  |
+----+
| 10 |
| 20 |
+----+
>>> df1.concat(df2, { how: "horizontal" })
shape: (2, 2)
+---+----+
| a | b  |
+---+----+
| 1 | 10 |
| 2 | 20 |
+---+----+

// 3. Diagonal Concatenation (mismatched columns):
>>> const df1 = $df.data({ a: [1, 2] })
>>> const df2 = $df.data({ b: [10, 20] })
>>> df1
shape: (2, 1)
+---+
| a |
+---+
| 1 |
| 2 |
+---+
>>> df2
shape: (2, 1)
+----+
| b  |
+----+
| 10 |
| 20 |
+----+
>>> df1.concat(df2, { how: "diagonal" })
shape: (4, 2)
+------+------+
| a    | b    |
+------+------+
| 1    | null |
| 2    | null |
| null | 10   |
| null | 20   |
+------+------+
```

---

## .drop()

Drops specified columns from the DataFrame.

### Signature
```typescript
df.drop<K extends keyof T>(...args: (K | K[])[]): DataFrame<Omit<T, K>>
```

### Parameters
- `args` ((K | K[])[]): Column names or arrays of column names to remove.

### Returns: `DataFrame`

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [1, 2], b: ["x", "y"] })
>>> df
shape: (2, 2)
+---+---+
| a | b |
+---+---+
| 1 | x |
| 2 | y |
+---+---+
>>> df.drop("b")
shape: (2, 1)
+---+
| a |
+---+
| 1 |
| 2 |
+---+
```

---

## .dropNulls()

Drops rows with null or undefined values.

### Signature
```typescript
df.dropNulls(subset?: string | string[]): DataFrame<T>
```

### Parameters
- `[subset]` (string | string[]): Column name or array of column names to check for nulls.

### Returns: `DataFrame`

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [1, null, 3], b: [null, 2, null] })
>>> df
shape: (3, 2)
+------+------+
| a    | b    |
+------+------+
| 1    | null |
| null | 2    |
| 3    | null |
+------+------+
>>> df.dropNulls()
shape: (2, 1)
+---+
| a |
+---+
| 1 |
| 3 |
+---+
```

## .equals()

Compares this DataFrame with another for equality. Checks shape, column names, column order, schemas, and row values.

### Signature
```typescript
df.equals<U extends RowRecord = any>(
  other: DataFrame<U>,
  {
    nullsEqual = true
  }: EqualsOptions = {}
): boolean
```

### Parameters
- `other` (DataFrame): The other DataFrame to compare with.
- `[options]` (EqualsOptions): Comparison configuration options.
- `[options.nullsEqual]` (boolean): Whether nulls / NaNs compare as equal. Default: `true`.

### Returns: `boolean`

### Types Referenced
- [`RowRecord`](#rowrecord)
- [`EqualsOptions`](#equalsoptions)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [1, 2], b: ["x", "y"] })
>>> df
shape: (2, 2)
+---+---+
| a | b |
+---+---+
| 1 | x |
| 2 | y |
+---+---+
>>> df.equals(df2)
true
```

## .explode()

Explodes an array column into multiple rows, replicating non-target row attributes.

### Signature
```typescript
df.explode(
  columns: IntoExpr | IntoExpr[],
  options?: ExplodeOptions
): DataFrame<any>
```

### Parameters
- `columns` (IntoExpr | IntoExpr[]): Target column expression or array column name to explode.
- `[options]` (ExplodeOptions): Configuration options for empty array and null handling.
- `[options.emptyAsNull]` (boolean): When `true`, converts empty arrays to `null` rows.
- `[options.keepNulls]` (boolean): When `true`, retains `null` array values during explosion.

### Returns: `DataFrame`

### Types Referenced
- [`IntoExpr`](#intoexpr)
- [`ExplodeOptions`](#explodeoptions)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5]] })
>>> df
shape: (2, 1)
+-----------+
| a         |
+-----------+
| [1, 2, 3] |
| [4, 5]    |
+-----------+
>>> df.explode("values")
shape: (2, 2)
+-------+--------+
| group | values |
+-------+--------+
| A     | 1      |
| A     | 2      |
+-------+--------+
```

---

## .fill()

Fills targeted values ("null", "nan", or "all") across columns using scalar values or statistical strategies.

### Signature
```typescript
df.fill(
  target: FillTarget,
  options: FillOptions | ValidScalarTypes | IExpr = {}
): DataFrame<T>
```

### Parameters
- `target` (FillTarget): Target type ("null", "nan", "all").
- `[options]` (FillOptions | ValidScalarTypes | IExpr): Configuration options or scalar/expression replacement.

### Returns: `DataFrame`

### Types Referenced
- [`FillTarget`](#filltarget)
- [`FillOptions`](#filloptions)
- [`ValidScalarTypes`](#validscalartypes)
- [`IExpr`](#iexpr)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [1, null, 3], b: [null, 2, null] })
>>> df
shape: (3, 2)
+------+------+
| a    | b    |
+------+------+
| 1    | null |
| null | 2    |
| 3    | null |
+------+------+
>>> df.fill("null", { value: 0 })
shape: (3, 1)
+---+
| a |
+---+
| 1 |
| 0 |
| 3 |
+---+
```

## .fillNull()

Fills null values across columns using scalar values or statistical strategies.

### Signature
```typescript
df.fillNull(options: FillNullOptions = {}): DataFrame<T>
```

### Parameters
- `[options]` (FillNullOptions): Configuration options for null replacement.
- `[options.value]` (any): Scalar replacement value or dict mapping column names to values.
- `[options.strategy]` (FillNullStrategy): Statistical filling strategy (`"zero"`, `"mean"`, `"min"`, `"max"`, `"forward"`, `"backward"`).
- `[options.limit]` (number): Maximum consecutive nulls to fill when using propagation strategies.

### Returns: `DataFrame`

### Types Referenced
- [`FillNullOptions`](#fillnulloptions)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [1, null, 3], b: [null, 2, null] })
>>> df
shape: (3, 2)
+------+------+
| a    | b    |
+------+------+
| 1    | null |
| null | 2    |
| 3    | null |
+------+------+
>>> df.fillNull({ value: 0 })
shape: (3, 1)
+---+
| a |
+---+
| 1 |
| 0 |
| 3 |
+---+
```

## .filter()

Filters rows matching boolean column expressions or predicate callbacks.

### Signature
```typescript
df.filter(...exprs: (IExpr | ((row: T) => any) | (IExpr | ((row: T) => any))[])[]): DataFrame<T>
```

### Parameters
- `exprs` ((IExpr | ((row: T) => any))[]): Expressions or predicate functions evaluated per row.

### Returns: `DataFrame`

### Types Referenced
- [`IExpr`](#iexpr)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [1, 2, 3], b: [10, 20, 30] })
>>> df
shape: (3, 2)
+---+----+
| a | b  |
+---+----+
| 1 | 10 |
| 2 | 20 |
| 3 | 30 |
+---+----+
>>> df.filter($df.col("a").gt(1))
shape: (2, 1)
+---+
| a |
+---+
| 2 |
| 3 |
+---+
```

## .groupBy()

Groups rows by key columns to prepare for aggregations.

### Signature
```typescript
df.groupBy<K extends keyof T>(keys: K | K[]): GroupedData<T, K>
```

### Parameters
- `keys` (K | K[]): Column name or array of key column names.

### Returns: `GroupedData`

### Types Referenced
- [`GroupedData`](#groupeddata)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ group: ["A", "A", "B"], val: [10, 20, 30] })
>>> df
shape: (3, 2)
+-------+-----+
| group | val |
+-------+-----+
| A     | 10  |
| A     | 20  |
| B     | 30  |
+-------+-----+
>>> df.groupBy("group").agg($df.col("val").sum().alias("sum"))
shape: (2, 2)
+-----+-----+
| cat | sum |
+-----+-----+
| A   | 30  |
| B   | 30  |
+-----+-----+
```

---

## .groupByDynamic()

Groups dynamically based on a time or integer index column over sliding / stepping windows.

### Signature
```typescript
df.groupByDynamic<K extends keyof T & string>(
  indexColumn: K | IntoExpr,
  options: GroupByDynamicOptions<T>
): GroupedData<T, K>
```

### Parameters
- `indexColumn` (any): The time/integer column or column expression to group on.
- `options` (any): Dynamic grouping configuration options (`every`, `period`, `offset`, `truncate`, `includeBoundaries`, `closed`, `label`, `by`, `startBy`, `checkSorted`).

### Returns: `GroupedData`

### Types Referenced
- [`IntoExpr`](#intoexpr)
- [`GroupByDynamicOptions`](#groupbydynamicoptions)
- [`GroupedData`](#groupeddata)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data([
...   { time: new Date("2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"), val: 10 },
...   { time: new Date("2024-01-01T12:00:00Z"), val: 20 },
...   { time: new Date("2024-01-02T00:00:00Z"), val: 30 }
... ])
>>> df
shape: (3, 2)
+--------------------------+-----+
| time                     | val |
+--------------------------+-----+
| 2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z | 10  |
| 2024-01-01T12:00:00.000Z | 20  |
| 2024-01-02T00:00:00.000Z | 30  |
+--------------------------+-----+
>>> df.groupByDynamic("time", { every: "1d", period: "1d" }).agg($df.col("val").sum().alias("daily_sum"))
shape: (2, 2)
+--------------------------+-----------+
| time                     | daily_sum |
+--------------------------+-----------+
| 2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z | 30        |
| 2024-01-02T00:00:00.000Z | 30        |
+--------------------------+-----------+
```

---

## .insertColumn()

```typescript
): DataFrame<any>
```

```typescript
+---+---+
| 1 | x |
| 2 | y |

+---+----+---+
```

```typescript
  row?: number,
  column?: number | string
): any
```

```typescript
shape: (2, 2)
```

## .iterColumns()

## .iterRows()

## .join()

Joins two DataFrames on key columns using a specified join strategy.

### Signature
```typescript
df.join<U extends RowRecord = any, R extends RowRecord = any>(
  other: DataFrame<U>,
  options: JoinOptions<T, U> = {}
): DataFrame<R>
```

### Parameters
- `other` (DataFrame): Right DataFrame to join with.
- `[options]` (JoinOptions, default: {}): Join configuration object.
- `[options.on]` (string | string[]): Join key column name or array of key column names that exist in both DataFrames.
- `[options.leftOn]` (string | string[]): Join key column(s) in the left DataFrame when key names differ.
- `[options.rightOn]` (string | string[]): Join key column(s) in the right DataFrame when key names differ.
- `[options.how]` (JoinType): Join strategy. Default `"inner"`. - `"inner"` — Only rows with matching keys in both DataFrames. - `"left"` — All left rows; unmatched right values are `null`. - `"right"` — All right rows; unmatched left values are `null`. - `"outer"` — All rows from both sides; unmatched values are `null`. - `"semi"` — Left rows that have a match in the right DataFrame (only left columns retained). - `"anti"` — Left rows that have **no** match in the right DataFrame (only left columns retained). - `"cross"` — Cartesian product pairing every left row with every right row (keyless).
- `[options.suffixes]` ([string, string]): Suffix tuple `[leftSuffix, rightSuffix]` appended to overlapping non-key column names (default `["", "_right"]`). Ignored for `"semi"` and `"anti"` joins.
- `[options.joinNulls]` (boolean): If `true`, null key values are treated as equal and will match each other across DataFrames. Default `false` (SQL-standard: `NULL != NULL`).
- `[options.coalesce]` (boolean): Coalescing behavior for join key columns. Default `true`. If `true`, coalesces join key values into left key columns and drops right key columns. If `false`, keeps join key columns separate.
- `[options.maintainOrder]` (JoinMaintainOrder | boolean): Row order preservation strategy. Default `"none"`. - `"none"` (or `false`) — No specific ordering is desired. - `"left"` (or `true`) — Preserves the order of the left DataFrame. - `"right"` — Preserves the order of the right DataFrame. - `"left_right"` — Preserves the order of the left DataFrame first, then the right. - `"right_left"` — Preserves the order of the right DataFrame first, then the left.

### Returns: `DataFrame`

### Types Referenced
- [`RowRecord`](#rowrecord)
- [`JoinOptions`](#joinoptions)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df1 = $df.data({ id: [1, 2], val: ["a", "b"] })
>>> const df2 = $df.data({ id: [1, 2], num: [100, 200] })
>>> df1
shape: (2, 2)
+----+-----+
| id | val |
+----+-----+
| 1  | a   |
| 2  | b   |
+----+-----+
>>> df2
shape: (2, 2)
+----+-----+
| id | num |
+----+-----+
| 1  | 100 |
| 2  | 200 |
+----+-----+
>>> df1.join(df2, { on: "id" })
shape: (2, 3)
+----+-----+-----+
| id | val | num |
+----+-----+-----+
| 1  | a   | 100 |
| 2  | b   | 200 |
+----+-----+-----+
```

---

## .joinAsof()

Performs an asof (as-of) join for inexact matching on ordered numeric or temporal key columns.

Similar to a left join, but instead of exact key equality, matches the nearest key row from the right DataFrame according to the selected `strategy` ("backward", "forward", or "nearest") and optional `tolerance`. Both DataFrames must be sorted in ascending order on their respective `on` / `leftOn` / `rightOn` join keys.

### Signature
```typescript
df.joinAsof<U extends RowRecord = any, R extends RowRecord = any>(
  other: DataFrame<U>,
  options: JoinAsofOptions<T, U>
): DataFrame<R>
```

### Parameters
- `other` (DataFrame): The right DataFrame to join with.
- `options` (JoinAsofOptions): Asof join configuration options.
- `[options.on]` (string): Column name to join on (must exist in both DataFrames and be sorted ascending).
- `[options.leftOn]` (string): Left DataFrame join key column name.
- `[options.rightOn]` (string): Right DataFrame join key column name.
- `[options.by]` (string | string[]): Optional exact-match group column(s) present in both DataFrames.
- `[options.leftBy]` (string | string[]): Group column(s) for exact key matching in left DataFrame.
- `[options.rightBy]` (string | string[]): Group column(s) for exact key matching in right DataFrame.
- `[options.strategy]` (JoinAsofStrategy): Match search strategy. Default `"backward"`. - `"backward"` — Matches the latest right row where `rightKey <= leftKey`. - `"forward"` — Matches the earliest right row where `rightKey >= leftKey`. - `"nearest"` — Matches the right row with the absolute nearest key value to `leftKey`.
- `[options.tolerance]` (number | string): Maximum allowed distance between left key and right key.
- `[options.allowExactMatches]` (boolean): Whether exact key matches are permitted. Default `true`.
- `[options.suffixes]` ([string, string]): Column name suffixes `[leftSuffix, rightSuffix]` to resolve name collisions. Default `["", "_right"]`.
- `[options.coalesce]` (boolean): Coalescing behavior for join key columns. Default `true`.
- `[options.checkSorted]` (boolean): Whether to verify that join keys are sorted ascending prior to matching. Default `true`.

### Returns: `A new DataFrame containing the joined results.`

### Types Referenced
- [`RowRecord`](#rowrecord)
- [`JoinAsofOptions`](#joinasofoptions)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const trades = $df.data([
...   { time: 1000, ticker: "AAPL", price: 150.0 },
...   { time: 1005, ticker: "AAPL", price: 150.5 },
...   { time: 1015, ticker: "AAPL", price: 151.0 }
... ])
>>> const quotes = $df.data([
...   { time: 998, ticker: "AAPL", bid: 149.9 },
...   { time: 1004, ticker: "AAPL", bid: 150.4 },
...   { time: 1010, ticker: "AAPL", bid: 150.8 }
... ])
>>> trades
shape: (3, 3)
+------+--------+-------+
| time | ticker | price |
+------+--------+-------+
| 1000 | AAPL   | 150.0 |
| 1005 | AAPL   | 150.5 |
| 1015 | AAPL   | 151.0 |
+------+--------+-------+
>>> quotes
shape: (3, 3)
+------+--------+-------+
| time | ticker | bid   |
+------+--------+-------+
| 998  | AAPL   | 149.9 |
| 1004 | AAPL   | 150.4 |
| 1010 | AAPL   | 150.8 |
+------+--------+-------+
>>> trades.joinAsof(quotes, { on: "time", by: "ticker" })
shape: (3, 4)
+------+--------+-------+-------+
| time | ticker | price | bid   |
+------+--------+-------+-------+
| 1000 | AAPL   | 150.0 | 149.9 |
| 1005 | AAPL   | 150.5 | 150.4 |
| 1015 | AAPL   | 151.0 | 150.8 |
+------+--------+-------+-------+
```

---

## .joinWhere()

Joins two DataFrames based on arbitrary expression predicates (non-equi joins).

Evaluates one or more boolean expressions across combined rows from both DataFrames. When column names collide between the two DataFrames, columns are suffixed according to `options.suffixes` (default `["", "_right"]`).

### Signature
```typescript
df.joinWhere<U extends RowRecord = any, R extends RowRecord = any>(
  other: DataFrame<U>,
  ...args: (IntoExpr | IntoExpr[] | JoinWhereOptions)[]
): DataFrame<R>
```

### Parameters
- `other` (DataFrame): The right DataFrame to join with.
- `args` (...(IntoExpr | IntoExpr[] | JoinWhereOptions)): Predicate expression(s), arrays of expressions, and an optional configuration options object (`{ how, suffixes }`).

### Returns: `DataFrame`

### Types Referenced
- [`RowRecord`](#rowrecord)
- [`IntoExpr`](#intoexpr)
- [`JoinWhereOptions`](#joinwhereoptions)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const east = $df.data([
...   { id: 100, dur: 120, rev: 12, cores: 2 },
...   { id: 101, dur: 140, rev: 14, cores: 8 },
...   { id: 102, dur: 160, rev: 16, cores: 4 }
... ])
>>> const west = $df.data([
...   { t_id: 404, time: 90, cost: 9, cores: 4 },
...   { t_id: 498, time: 130, cost: 13, cores: 2 },
...   { t_id: 676, time: 150, cost: 15, cores: 1 },
...   { t_id: 742, time: 170, cost: 16, cores: 4 }
... ])
>>> east
shape: (3, 4)
+-----+-----+-----+-------+
| id  | dur | rev | cores |
+-----+-----+-----+-------+
| 100 | 120 | 12  | 2     |
| 101 | 140 | 14  | 8     |
| 102 | 160 | 16  | 4     |
+-----+-----+-----+-------+
>>> west
shape: (4, 4)
+------+------+------+-------+
| t_id | time | cost | cores |
+------+------+------+-------+
| 404  | 90   | 9    | 4     |
| 498  | 130  | 13   | 2     |
| 676  | 150  | 15   | 1     |
| 742  | 170  | 16   | 4     |
+------+------+------+-------+
```

## .limit()

Limits the output to N rows starting from offset.

### Signature
```typescript
df.limit(
  n: number,
  {
    offset = 0,
    from = "start"
  }: LimitOptions = {}
): DataFrame<T>
```

### Parameters
- `n` (number): Maximum number of rows to take.
- `[options]` (LimitOptions): Offset and slice direction options.
- `[options.offset]` (number): Number of rows to skip before taking `n` rows (default 0).
- `[options.from]` (LimitPosition): Slice direction starting point (`"start"` or `"end"`). Default `"start"`.

### Returns: `DataFrame`

### Types Referenced
- [`LimitOptions`](#limitoptions)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [1, 2, 3] })
>>> df
shape: (3, 1)
+---+
| a |
+---+
| 1 |
| 2 |
| 3 |
+---+
>>> df.limit(2, { offset: 1 })
shape: (2, 1)
+----+
| a  |
+----+
| 20 |
| 30 |
+----+
```

## .pivot()

Pivots columns from long format to a wide datagrid structure.

### Signature
```typescript
df.pivot<U extends RowRecord = any>(config: PivotOptions<T>): DataFrame<U>
```

### Parameters
- `config` (any): Pivot table configuration options.
- `config.index` (string | string[]): Key column(s) to use as new DataFrame rows.
- `config.columns` (string): Column whose distinct values become new wide column headers.
- `config.values` (string): Column whose cell values populate the pivoted grid cells.
- `[config.agg]` (AggFn | string): Aggregation function to apply when multiple values exist for a cell.

### Returns: `DataFrame`

### Types Referenced
- [`RowRecord`](#rowrecord)
- [`PivotOptions`](#pivotoptions)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ year: [2020, 2020, 2021, 2021], month: ["Jan", "Feb", "Jan", "Feb"], revenue: [100, 150, 120, 180] })
>>> df
shape: (4, 3)
+------+-------+---------+
| year | month | revenue |
+------+-------+---------+
| 2020 | Jan   | 100     |
| 2020 | Feb   | 150     |
| 2021 | Jan   | 120     |
| 2021 | Feb   | 180     |
+------+-------+---------+
>>> df.pivot({ index: "year", columns: "month", values: "revenue" })
shape: (2, 3)
+------+-----+-----+
| year | Jan | Feb |
+------+-----+-----+
| 2020 | 100 | 150 |
| 2021 | 120 | 180 |
+------+-----+-----+
```

## .sort()

Sorts DataFrame rows by one or more column expressions or custom sorters.

### Signature
```typescript
df.sort(config?: SortOptions<T>): DataFrame<T>
```

### Parameters
- `[config]` (SortOptions<T>): Sort configuration options.
- `config.by` (keyof T | (keyof T)[] | IExpr | IExpr[]): Column name(s) or expression(s) to sort by.
- `[config.descending]` (boolean | boolean[]): Sort order boolean or array of booleans per key (default `false`).
- `[config.nullsLast]` (boolean): When `true` (default), places nulls at the end of sorted output.
- `[config.custom]` (Partial<Record<keyof T, (a: any, b: any) => number>>): Optional dictionary mapping column names to custom comparator functions.

### Returns: `DataFrame`

### Types Referenced
- [`SortOptions`](#sortoptions)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [1, 2, 3], b: [10, 20, 30] })
>>> df
shape: (3, 2)
+---+----+
| a | b  |
+---+----+
| 1 | 10 |
| 2 | 20 |
| 3 | 30 |
+---+----+
>>> df.sort({ by: "a", descending: true })
shape: (3, 2)
+---+----+
| a | b  |
+---+----+
| 3 | 30 |
| 2 | 20 |
| 1 | 10 |
+---+----+
```

## .transpose()

Transposes rows into columns and columns into rows.

### Signature
```typescript
df.transpose(
  {
    includeHeader = false,
    headerName = "column",
    columnNames
  }: TransposeOptions = {}
): DataFrame<any>
```

### Parameters
- `[options]` (TransposeOptions): Transpose layout options.
- `[options.includeHeader]` (boolean): When `true`, includes original column names as a new header column (default `false`).
- `[options.headerName]` (string): Name of the header column when `includeHeader` is `true` (default `"column"`).
- `[options.columnNames]` (string | Iterable<string>): Column name or iterable of strings to use as transposed column headers.

### Returns: `DataFrame`

### Types Referenced
- [`TransposeOptions`](#transposeoptions)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ year: [2020, 2020, 2021, 2021], month: ["Jan", "Feb", "Jan", "Feb"], revenue: [100, 150, 120, 180] })
>>> df
shape: (4, 3)
+------+-------+---------+
| year | month | revenue |
+------+-------+---------+
| 2020 | Jan   | 100     |
| 2020 | Feb   | 150     |
| 2021 | Jan   | 120     |
| 2021 | Feb   | 180     |
+------+-------+---------+
>>> df.transpose({ includeHeader: true, headerName: "metric" })
shape: (2, 3)
+--------+----------+----------+
| metric | column_0 | column_1 |
+--------+----------+----------+
| q1     | 100      | 500      |
| q2     | 120      | 600      |
+--------+----------+----------+
```

## .unpivot()

Unpivots a wide DataFrame into a long format structure.

### Signature
```typescript
df.unpivot<U extends RowRecord = any>(config: UnpivotOptions<T>): DataFrame<U>
```

### Parameters
- `config` (UnpivotOptions<T>): Unpivot configuration options.
- `config.idVars` (keyof T | (keyof T)[]): Key column(s) to retain as identifier variables.
- `config.valueVars` (keyof T | (keyof T)[]): Column(s) to unpivot into variable-value pairs.
- `[config.varName]` (string): Name for the new variable column holding old column headers (default `"variable"`).
- `[config.valueName]` (string): Name for the new value column holding cell values (default `"value"`).

### Returns: `DataFrame`

### Types Referenced
- [`RowRecord`](#rowrecord)
- [`UnpivotOptions`](#unpivotoptions)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ year: [2020, 2020, 2021, 2021], month: ["Jan", "Feb", "Jan", "Feb"], revenue: [100, 150, 120, 180] })
>>> df
shape: (4, 3)
+------+-------+---------+
| year | month | revenue |
+------+-------+---------+
| 2020 | Jan   | 100     |
| 2020 | Feb   | 150     |
| 2021 | Jan   | 120     |
| 2021 | Feb   | 180     |
+------+-------+---------+
>>> df.unpivot({ idVars: "metric", valueVars: ["q1", "q2"], varName: "quarter", valueName: "val" })
shape: (4, 3)
+--------+---------+-----+
| metric | quarter | val |
+--------+---------+-----+
| sales  | q1      | 100 |
| sales  | q2      | 120 |
| clicks | q1      | 500 |
| clicks | q2      | 600 |
+--------+---------+-----+
```

---

## .unstack()

Unstacks selected columns into multiple wide columns of size `step`. Reshapes data from long to wide format without aggregation.

### Signature
```typescript
df.unstack(
  columns: IntoExpr | IntoExpr[],
  options: UnstackOptions
): DataFrame<any>
```

### Parameters
- `columns` (any): Column name(s) or selector(s) to unstack.
- `options` (any): Unstack configuration options (`step`, `how`, `fillValues`).

### Returns: `DataFrame`

### Types Referenced
- [`IntoExpr`](#intoexpr)
- [`UnstackOptions`](#unstackoptions)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [1, 2, 3] })
>>> df
shape: (3, 1)
+---+
| a |
+---+
| 1 |
| 2 |
| 3 |
+---+
>>> df.unstack("a", { step: 2, how: "horizontal" })
shape: (2, 2)
+-----+------+
| a_0 | a_1  |
+-----+------+
| 1   | 2    |
| 3   | null |
+-----+------+
```

---

## .width

Gets width (total column count) of the DataFrame.

### Signature
```typescript
df.width: number
```

### Returns: `Number of columns.`

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [1, 2], b: ["x", "y"] })
>>> df
shape: (2, 2)
+---+---+
| a | b |
+---+---+
| 1 | x |
| 2 | y |
+---+---+
>>> df.width
2
```

## .withColumns()

Adds new columns or updates existing ones using column expressions.

### Signature
```typescript
df.withColumns(...args: (string | IExpr | Record<string, any> | (string | IExpr | Record<string, any>)[])[]): DataFrame<any>
```

### Parameters
- `args` ((string | IExpr | Record<string, any> | (string | IExpr | Record<string, any>)[])[]): Expressions or field objects defining column calculations.

### Returns: `DataFrame`

### Types Referenced
- [`IExpr`](#iexpr)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [1, 2], b: ["x", "y"] })
>>> df
shape: (2, 2)
+---+---+
| a | b |
+---+---+
| 1 | x |
| 2 | y |
+---+---+
>>> df.withColumns($df.col("a").mul(10).alias("a_x10"))
shape: (2, 3)
+---+---+-------+
| a | b | a_x10 |
+---+---+-------+
| 1 | x | 10    |
| 2 | y | 20    |
+---+---+-------+
```

## .withRowIndex()

Appends an incremental index column.

### Signature
```typescript
df.withRowIndex(
  name: string = "index",
  offset: number = 0
): DataFrame<any>
```

### Parameters
- `[name]` (string): Name of index column (default "index").
- `[offset]` (number): Starting numeric index offset (default 0).

### Returns: `DataFrame`

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [1, 2], b: ["x", "y"] })
>>> df
shape: (2, 2)
+---+---+
| a | b |
+---+---+
| 1 | x |
| 2 | y |
+---+---+
>>> df.withRowIndex("idx")
shape: (2, 3)
+-----+---+---+
| idx | a | b |
+-----+---+---+
| 0   | 1 | x |
| 1   | 2 | y |
+-----+---+---+
```

## .writeCsv()

Writes DataFrame to CSV format string or file/stream target.

### Signature
```typescript
df.writeCsv(
  file?: string | { write: (str: string) => void },
  options: WriteCSVOptions = {}
): string
```

### Parameters
- `[file]` (string | { write: (str: string) => void }): Target file path or writable stream target (optional).
- `[options]` (WriteCSVOptions): CSV formatting options.
- `[options.delimiter]` (string): Column delimiter character (default `","`).
- `[options.header]` (boolean): When `true` (default), includes column header row.
- `[options.quoteChar]` (string): Character used to enclose fields containing special characters (default `'"'`).

### Returns: `string`

### Types Referenced
- [`WriteCSVOptions`](#writecsvoptions)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [1, 2], b: ["x", "y"] })
>>> df
shape: (2, 2)
+---+---+
| a | b |
+---+---+
| 1 | x |
| 2 | y |
+---+---+
>>> df.writeCsv()
"a,b\n1,x"
```

---

## .writeJson()

Writes DataFrame rows to JSON format string or file/stream target.

### Signature
```typescript
df.writeJson(
  file?: string | { write: (str: string) => void },
  {
    format = "json",
    replacerOptions
  }: WriteJSONOptions = {}
): string
```

### Parameters
- `[file]` (string | { write: (str: string) => void }): Target file path or writable stream target (optional).
- `[options]` (WriteJSONOptions): JSON formatting and replacer options.
- `[options.format]` (JSONFormat): JSON output format structure (`"json"` or `"ndjson"`). Default `"json"`.
- `[options.replacerOptions]` (SafeJsonReplacerOptions): Serialization options for custom type handling.
- `[options.replacerOptions.formatDate]` ((v: Date) => string): Custom formatter function for Date objects. Ignored if `onDate` is specified.
- `[options.replacerOptions.bigintStrategy]` ("string" | "number"): Convert BigInts to numeric strings or numbers if safe. Default `"string"`.
- `[options.replacerOptions.onBigInt]` ((v: bigint) => any): Custom serialization override for BigInt values.
- `[options.replacerOptions.onTypedArray]` ((v: any) => any): Custom serialization override for TypedArray values.
- `[options.replacerOptions.onSet]` ((v: Set<any>) => any): Custom serialization override for Set objects.
- `[options.replacerOptions.onMap]` ((v: Map<any, any>) => any): Custom serialization override for Map objects.
- `[options.replacerOptions.onRegExp]` ((v: RegExp) => any): Custom serialization override for RegExp objects.
- `[options.replacerOptions.onDate]` ((v: Date) => any): Custom serialization override for Date objects. Takes precedence over `formatDate`.
- `[options.replacerOptions.onError]` ((v: Error) => any): Custom serialization override for Error objects. Prevents empty `{}` output.
- `[options.replacerOptions.onURLSearchParams]` ((v: URLSearchParams) => any): Custom serialization override for URLSearchParams objects.
- `[options.replacerOptions.onCustom]` ((this: any, k: string, v: any) => any): Catch-all serialization override for custom types. Runs after native type checks.
- `[options.replacerOptions.handleCircular]` (boolean): If `true`, handles circular references by replacing them instead of throwing.
- `[options.replacerOptions.onCircular]` ((this: any, k: string, v: any) => any): Custom fallback when a circular reference is found. Default `"[Circular]"`.
- `[options.replacerOptions.voidBigIntReplacement]` (boolean): If `true`, disables the default safe serialization for BigInt values.
- `[options.replacerOptions.voidTypedArrayReplacement]` (boolean): If `true`, disables the default safe serialization for TypedArray values.
- `[options.replacerOptions.voidSetReplacement]` (boolean): If `true`, disables the default safe serialization for Set objects.
- `[options.replacerOptions.voidMapReplacement]` (boolean): If `true`, disables the default safe serialization for Map objects.
- `[options.replacerOptions.voidRegExpReplacement]` (boolean): If `true`, disables the default safe serialization for RegExp objects.
- `[options.replacerOptions.voidDateReplacement]` (boolean): If `true`, disables the default safe serialization for Date objects.
- `[options.replacerOptions.replacer]` (((this: any, k: string, v: any) => any) | (string | number)[] | null): Custom replacer function or array whitelist that runs first for pre-processing.

### Returns: `string`

### Types Referenced
- [`WriteJSONOptions`](#writejsonoptions)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [1, 2], b: ["x", "y"] })
>>> df
shape: (2, 2)
+---+---+
| a | b |
+---+---+
| 1 | x |
| 2 | y |
+---+---+
>>> df.writeJson()
'[{"a":1,"b":"x"}]'
```

---

## .agg()

Aggregates grouped partitions using aggregation column expressions.

### Signature
```typescript
df.groupBy(...).agg<U extends RowRecord = any>(...exprs: (IExpr | any)[]): DataFrame<U>
```

### Parameters
- `exprs` (any): One or more aggregation column expressions.

### Returns: `DataFrame`

### Types Referenced
- [`RowRecord`](#rowrecord)
- [`IExpr`](#iexpr)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ group: ["A", "A", "B"], val: [10, 20, 30] })
>>> df
shape: (3, 2)
+-------+-----+
| group | val |
+-------+-----+
| A     | 10  |
| A     | 20  |
| B     | 30  |
+-------+-----+
>>> df.groupBy("group").agg($df.col("val").sum().alias("sum_val"))
shape: (2, 2)
+-------+---------+
| group | sum_val |
+-------+---------+
| A     | 30      |
| B     | 30      |
+-------+---------+
```

## .toDataframe()

Converts group keys back into a single distinct DataFrame without aggregations.

### Signature
```typescript

```

### Returns: `DataFrame`

### Types Referenced
- [`RowRecord`](#rowrecord)

### Examples
```typescript

>>> df
shape: (3, 2)
+-------+-----+
| group | val |
+-------+-----+
| A     | 10  |
| A     | 20  |
| B     | 30  |
+-------+-----+
>>> df.groupBy("group").toDataframe()

+-------+
| group |
+-------+
| A     |
| B     |
+-------+
```

## coalesce()

Returns the first non-null value among the specified expressions.

### Signature
```typescript
$df.coalesce(...exprs: (IExpr | ValidScalarTypes | (IExpr | ValidScalarTypes)[])[]): ColumnExpr<any>
```

### Parameters
- `exprs` (...(IExpr | ValidScalarTypes | (IExpr | ValidScalarTypes)[])[]): The list of expressions or columns to coalesce.

### Returns: `ColumnExpr<any>`

### Types Referenced
- [`IExpr`](#iexpr)
- [`ValidScalarTypes`](#validscalartypes)
- [`ColumnExpr`](#columnexpr)

### Examples
```typescript
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [1, null, 3], b: [null, 2, null] })
>>> df
shape: (3, 2)
+------+------+
| a    | b    |
+------+------+
| 1    | null |
| null | 2    |
| 3    | null |
+------+------+
>>> df.select($df.coalesce($df.col("a"), $df.col("b"), $df.lit(3)).alias("coalesced"))
shape: (3, 1)
+-----------+
| coalesced |
+-----------+
| 1         |
| 2         |
| 3         |
+-----------+
```
